correctness.rationale: Every maximizing Fourier frequency can be modulated to zero, mass-normalized to one, and averaged over the stabilizer of the two-axis set; strict convexity of counting ℓ4 forces all equality functions to lie in the two-orbit subspace. Fourier character orthogonality gives multiplicities 1, 2(q−1), (q−1)^2 and polynomial P=1+2(q−1)|1−x|^4+(q−1)^2|1−2x|^4. Its unique minimizer x=(1+(q−1)^(1/3))/(1+2(q−1)^(1/3)) gives the exact formula. The group exists over all prime powers. The public proof treats full equality, sign, boundaries and asymptotics. The packaged stdlib checker passed 734 supplementary checks including extension field q=9; finite checks are not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: The published general synthesis theorem (arXiv:2609.25404, Section 4) requires affine transitivity and supplies the indicator as optimizer. The two-line cross has a separate origin orbit for q>2. Full cross-specific Fourier extension statements optimize a different ratio and have different equality functions. None of the inspected exact results implies the nontransitive sharp ℓ∞/ℓ4 coefficient and signed two-level optimizer. The remaining risk is an unindexed equivalent two-orbit minimization.

value.rationale: Computing the sharp synthesis constant for a crossing pair of coordinate lines is motivated by the recent exact-transitive-affine synthesis theorem, whose hypothesis fails at the distinguished intersection. The nontrivial two-orbit program leads to an all-prime-power sharp constant and full complex equality classification, and exposes a signed origin-weight transition invisible to indicator tests. It gives a natural exact harmonic-analysis invariant, not an arbitrary finite slice or restatement of the different extension problem.
